page: Microsoft Azure F32amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs, utilizing the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 3780 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong processing capabilities, with single-core stress-ng performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core stress-ng performance and PassMark CPU scores place the server in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks consistently rank in the top 25%. Database operations on PassMark achieve top-tier status, and Redis SET operations register in the top 25%.

For machine learning workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds for small 135M LLM models, and strong performance for medium 7B models. However, performance drops to average levels for large 70B models, highlighting a tradeoff when running massive parameter models without dedicated GPU acceleration. Given the high memory density, fast local NVMe storage, and strong single-core CPU performance, this server is suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data processing, and medium-scale language model inference.
